briefs.flowNote: Money is going into chips and growth premarket on Nvidia's beat: semiconductors (SMH +1.8%), high-growth tech (ARKK +1.3%) and technology (XLK +1.0%) lead, with software (IGV +0.5%) steadying after Tuesday's −3.3%. bigPicture: Nvidia passed the test the market feared, Kress's first report, but chip pops were sold at the open Monday and Tuesday; today shows whether money holds a gap after the S&P's fourth straight loss.

Rates are the cap: Waller argues for 50 bp in December while futures price 25; real yields are up, gold is at a one-year low and the dollar is firmer. Leveraged AI builders and long-duration software feel it first.
Consumer beats lean on tariff refunds: Lowe's and Target are sold, while TJX's cleaner beat is bought.
Geopolitics stays in the background: Iranian drone attacks on Kuwait, stalled talks, Trump meeting Xi and Putin Thursday; oil stays soft (WTI 84.48) on the IEA's surplus.
snapshot.takeaway: Nvidia gave chips a real reason to gap up, but two days of sold opening pops say wait: if NVDA and SMH hold their premarket highs on the first retest, the relief has buyers; if they slip back under yesterday's highs, it is the same fade. The 2:00 PM minutes decide the afternoon after Waller's 50 bp talk.
